obligations.note: The statement-delivery error path now passes the payee account number, a payments NPI field, into AppLog.error with no mask at the call site. The registered LOG-1 test is sample coverage only, so a green run does not show this error path is free of unmasked NPI.
The diff only changes that error log line. Every state-changing method in service.py still records actor, action, target, and time, and test_sampled_operations_are_audited passed on the head commit.
Ticket CHG-24888 is approved by change manager Grace Kim before review and lists payments.service, the component for the only file changed.
Sofia Santos, a payments change approver and not the author Linh Nguyen, approved the code review.
The code-review approval names head commit b7c14ece1e64e799086ae6d5fb626cf9e777a8ea, which is the only commit on the change.
records/ci/run.json records a successful payments suite on that head commit, and the JUnit report shows 172 tests with the AUD-1 and LOG-1 control tests unskipped and passing.
apps/baseline-payments/payments/service.py is component payments.service with security_sensitive false, so no security review is required.
The change does not touch a protected path under controls/, control tests, or ci/.

The LOG-1 deviation has no approved exception for this component. EXC-0167 is limited to mortgage.logging and a legacy import of a masked last-4, and it does not cover payments statement-delivery logs.
Acceptance-ledger entries cover payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, and mortgage files, none of which this change modifies.

summary: The change adds the payee account number to the statement-delivery failure log. Account number is nonpublic personal information, and LOG-1 forbids it on error paths. The logging control test is only a sample, and no in-scope exception authorizes the deviation. Process records for the ticket, independent approval, final-commit tests, and unchanged prior evidence are in order, but the logging breach requires rejection.
